learningGoals.title: Read every field of a failover group status that matters on call
Distinguish group-level health from per-site health
Turn a status read into an exit code a check script can act on

config.title: brstatus — the one-screen status reader
config.description: Complete a small Python tool that turns the JSON of the `orders` MysqlFailoverGroup into a header line, one line per site, and a verdict with a matching exit code. Three functions are stubbed. The interesting one is the rule that decides whether a site is serving reads — because it is not the same rule for a reader as it is for a primary candidate.
config.instructions:
## How this works

`orders` is your three-site failover group: `iad` and `pdx` are `primary-candidate`, `reader` is `read-only`. From Unit 2 onward you will look at its status constantly, and `kubectl get mysqlfailovergroup orders -o json` is 400 lines. `brstatus` squeezes it to one screen:

```
orders/bloodraven-playground  active=iad  ready=True  degraded=False(Healthy)
SITE    ROLE               STATE      REPL  LAG      SERVING
iad     primary-candidate  writable   no    unknown  no
pdx     primary-candidate  read-only  yes   0s       yes
reader  read-only          read-only  yes   0s       yes
VERDICT: OK
```

And it exits with a code you can act on:

| Exit | Verdict | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `OK` | the `Degraded` condition is not `True` |
| 1 | `DEGRADED` | `Degraded` is `True` and `status.activeSite` is set |
| 2 | `CRITICAL` | `Degraded` is `True` and `status.activeSite` is empty |
| 3 | — | the input was not one MysqlFailoverGroup |

Exit 2 is the shape of split brain and of no-primary: in both, no site is the unambiguous authority, so `status.activeSite` is empty.

Everything runs against JSON fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`. No cluster is needed to finish the code.

## Your tasks

Open `starter/brstatus.py`. Run it first, before you change anything:

```bash
python starter/brstatus.py tests/fixtures/orders-healthy.json
```

It runs. It is also wrong in three ways, and each one is a `TODO`.

**TODO A — `format_lag`.** `status.sites[].secondsBehindSource` is a pointer, and it is absent whenever the operator has no replication reading for that site: the active primary, a site it could not poll, a replica whose threads are stopped. Return `"unknown"` when it is absent or null and `"<n>s"` otherwise. The starter prints `0s` for absent, which is how a detached replica ends up looking perfectly caught up.

**TODO B — `is_serving`.** Decide whether a site is currently behind `mysql-orders-replicas`, the group read endpoint. That Service selects on three labels — instance, `role=replica`, and `healthy=yes` — and the operator's rule for stamping `healthy` depends on the site's role.

For a site whose role is `read-only`, all five must hold together:

1. `sourceConvergenceState` is `Converged`
2. `replicating` is true
3. `secondsBehindSource` is present (not null)
4. `canonical_host(sourceHost)` equals `expected_source_host(...)` for the active site — a replica chained off another replica does not count
5. `secondsBehindSource` is at or under `effective_readonly_max_lag(spec)`

For **every other role**, `healthy=yes` as soon as `state` is `writable` or `read-only`. There is no lag gate on those sites at all. That asymmetry is real and it is the point of this project.

**TODO C — `verdict`.** Return `(word, exit_code)` from the table above. Read the `Degraded` condition the operator already wrote — its `reason` is one of `Healthy`, `Degraded`, `SplitBrain`, `NoPrimary`, `TotalLoss`, or a replication reason such as `ReplicationLagging`. Do not re-derive group health from the site rows.

Then do the cluster half: with `orders` up, capture a live status and read it with your own tool.

```bash
mkdir -p artefacts
kubectl -n bloodraven-playground get mysqlfailovergroup orders -o json > artefacts/orders-live.json
python starter/brstatus.py artefacts/orders-live.json
```

## What the scaffolding is for

You do not have to write any of this, but you do have to call it:

- `site_role(site_spec)` applies the CRD default — `spec.sites[].role` is optional and defaults to `primary-candidate`.
- `effective_max_lag(spec)` is `spec.replication.maxLagSeconds`, defaulting to 300.
- `effective_readonly_max_lag(spec)` is `spec.replication.readOnlyMaxLagSeconds`. It has **no default of its own**: absent inherits `maxLagSeconds`, but an explicit `0` is meaningful and means the reader must report zero lag. `.get("readOnlyMaxLagSeconds") or ...` gets that wrong.
- `condition(status, "Degraded")` pulls one entry out of `status.conditions`.
- `canonical_host()` and `expected_source_host()` compare replication source hosts the way the operator does — lowercased, `:3306` stripped, trailing dot stripped.
- Inside `is_serving`, two guards are already written for you: an empty `status.activeSite` sheds every endpoint, and the active site itself is never serving, because it carries `role=primary` rather than `role=replica`.
- `render()` sizes the columns. Print whatever you like around it; the tests parse cells, not widths.

## Expected output

With all three TODOs done, `tests/fixtures/orders-reader-soaking.json` — where `reader` is 300 seconds behind a 30 second threshold — must produce this, and exit **0**:

```
orders/bloodraven-playground  active=iad  ready=True  degraded=False(Healthy)
SITE    ROLE               STATE      REPL  LAG      SERVING
iad     primary-candidate  writable   no    unknown  no
pdx     primary-candidate  read-only  yes   0s       yes
reader  read-only          read-only  yes   300s     no
VERDICT: OK
```

And `tests/fixtures/orders-candidate-lagging.json` — where `pdx` is 300 seconds behind the same threshold — must exit **1**, with `pdx` still marked `SERVING yes`.

One site 300 seconds behind, two opposite answers. Work out why before you write the code.

Run everything:

```bash
python tests/test_brstatus.py
```

## Rules

- Standard library only. No `kubernetes` client, no `pyyaml`, no network.
- Do not edit anything in `tests/`. Fixtures and checks are the grader's copy.
- Keep the function names `format_lag`, `is_serving` and `verdict` — a structural check looks for them.
- Every threshold comes from the object you were handed. Do not hard-code `30`; the shipped default is 300 and the playground overrides it.
- `secondsBehindSource` of `0` and `secondsBehindSource` absent are different facts. Never collapse them.

starterCells.content:
## The contract

`brstatus.py <group.json>` prints:

1. a header — `<name>/<namespace>  active=<site|none>  ready=<True|False>  degraded=<status>(<reason>)`
2. an `ALERT: <message>` line when `Degraded` is `True` and carries a message
3. a table with the columns `SITE ROLE STATE REPL LAG SERVING`
4. a last line `VERDICT: OK|DEGRADED|CRITICAL`

and exits `0`, `1`, `2`, or `3` for unreadable input.

Cells: `LAG` is `unknown` or `<n>s`. `REPL` and `SERVING` are `yes` or `no`. `STATE` is one of `writable`, `read-only`, `unreachable`, `unknown`.

## The fixtures

All seven are real-shaped `MysqlFailoverGroup` objects for `orders` in `bloodraven-playground`, with `spec.replication.maxLagSeconds: 30` as the playground sets it.

| Fixture | What it holds | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `orders-healthy.json` | one writable site, both followers caught up | 0 |
| `orders-reader-soaking.json` | the `read-only` reader is 300s behind | 0 |
| `orders-candidate-lagging.json` | the `primary-candidate` replica is 300s behind | 1 |
| `orders-reader-detached.json` | reader not replicating, lag absent, wrong source | 0 |
| `orders-zero-readonly-lag.json` | `readOnlyMaxLagSeconds: 0`, both followers 30s behind | 0 |
| `orders-no-primary.json` | both core sites read-only, none unreachable | 2 |
| `orders-split-brain.json` | two writable core sites, authority ambiguous | 2 |

Two of them are 300 seconds behind and disagree about what that means. That is the exercise.

steps.title: Run the starter and find the lie
steps.description: Run `python starter/brstatus.py tests/fixtures/orders-healthy.json` before changing anything. It prints a clean table. Look at the `iad` row: it is the writable primary, it reports no replication lag at all, and the tool prints `0s`. Note which rows you already do not believe.
steps.completionCriteria: `python starter/brstatus.py tests/fixtures/orders-healthy.json` runs to completion and its `iad` row shows `0s` in the LAG column.

steps.title: TODO A — absent lag is not zero lag
steps.description: Complete `format_lag`. Return `"unknown"` when `secondsBehindSource` is absent or null, `"<n>s"` otherwise. `site_status.get("secondsBehindSource") or 0` is the trap: it turns both null and zero into zero.
steps.completionCriteria: For `tests/fixtures/orders-healthy.json` the `iad` row shows `unknown` in the LAG column and the `pdx` row shows `0s`.

steps.title: TODO B — the reader rule and the candidate rule are different rules
steps.description: Complete `is_serving`. Apply the five conjuncts to a `read-only` site, using `effective_readonly_max_lag(spec)` as the threshold. Apply no lag gate at all to any other role — a `primary-candidate` replica in state `read-only` is serving no matter how far behind it is.
steps.completionCriteria: For `tests/fixtures/orders-reader-soaking.json` the `reader` row shows `no` in the SERVING column and the `pdx` row shows `yes`; for `tests/fixtures/orders-candidate-lagging.json` the `pdx` row shows `yes` in the SERVING column.

steps.title: TODO C — the verdict and the exit code
steps.description: Complete `verdict` from the `Degraded` condition and `status.activeSite`. The operator already evaluated the cross-site table on every poll and wrote the answer down; your job is to read it, not to recompute it.
steps.completionCriteria: `brstatus.py` exits 0 on `orders-healthy.json`, 1 on `orders-candidate-lagging.json`, and 2 on `orders-no-primary.json`, whose last line reads `VERDICT: CRITICAL`.

steps.title: Point it at the real orders
steps.description: With the playground up, capture a live status and read it with your own tool: `kubectl -n bloodraven-playground get mysqlfailovergroup orders -o json > artefacts/orders-live.json`, then `python starter/brstatus.py artefacts/orders-live.json`. This is the artefact you will re-read in every later unit.
steps.completionCriteria: A file `artefacts/orders-live.json` exists, contains the string `"kind": "MysqlFailoverGroup"`, and `python starter/brstatus.py artefacts/orders-live.json` exits 0, 1 or 2 rather than 3.

steps.title: Write down the inversion
steps.description: Two fixtures have a site 300 seconds behind a 30 second threshold. One exits 0, one exits 1. Add a comment at the bottom of `starter/brstatus.py`, on a line starting `# READER-LAG:`, naming the fixture that exits 0 and saying in one sentence why a lagging reader leaves the group healthy while a lagging primary candidate does not.
steps.completionCriteria: `starter/brstatus.py` contains a line beginning `# READER-LAG:` that names `orders-reader-soaking.json`.

rubric.criterion: The verdict and exit code come from the group's conditions
rubric.description: `verdict` reads the `Degraded` condition out of `status.conditions` and combines it with `status.activeSite` to return exactly `("OK", 0)`, `("DEGRADED", 1)` or `("CRITICAL", 2)`. Full marks require that no per-site field — lag, replicating, state — is consulted inside `verdict`. Award 14 if the three codes are right but group health is partly re-derived from the site rows; award 0 if any fixture returns the wrong code.

rubric.criterion: Reader endpoint eligibility is role-aware and complete
rubric.description: `is_serving` branches on `site_role(...)`. The `read-only` branch tests all five conjuncts — converged source, replicating, non-null lag, canonical direct source host, and lag at or under `effective_readonly_max_lag(spec)`. Every other role is served on `state` alone with no lag gate. Award 14 if the five conjuncts are right but the same gate is wrongly applied to `primary-candidate` sites, or if a conjunct is missing; award 0 if the reader threshold is `effective_max_lag` instead.

rubric.criterion: Absent lag is distinguished from zero lag
rubric.description: `format_lag` returns `unknown` for an absent or null `secondsBehindSource` and `<n>s` otherwise, and `is_serving` treats a null lag as disqualifying rather than as `0`. Award 8 if only one of the two places is right.

rubric.criterion: The tool was run against the live orders group
rubric.description: `artefacts/orders-live.json` is present, is a single `MysqlFailoverGroup` captured from the running playground rather than a copied fixture (its `metadata.creationTimestamp`, `metadata.uid` and `status.sites[].lastSeen` are populated), and the submission shows `brstatus` output for it.

rubric.criterion: Craft: the output stays one screen and the code survives a thin status
rubric.description: The header, table and `VERDICT:` line are intact and readable, absent optional fields (`state`, `secondsBehindSource`, `conditions`, `sourceHost`) produce a cell rather than a traceback, unreadable input exits 3 with a message on stderr, and the three completed functions carry a comment a colleague could follow — naming the rule, not restating the code. Deduct for debug prints left in the output, for hard-coded thresholds, and for rewriting scaffolding that was already correct.

testCases.name: healthy_group_summary
testCases.code:
import pathlib, sys
_here = pathlib.Path.cwd().resolve()
_tests = None
for _p in [_here, *_here.parents]:
    for _c in (_p / 'tests', _p):
        if (_c / '_harness.py').is_file() and (_c / 'test_brstatus.py').is_file():
            _tests = _c
            break
    if _tests:
        break
assert _tests, 'cannot find the project tests/ directory'
sys.path.insert(0, str(_tests))
from test_brstatus import test_healthy_group_summary
test_healthy_group_summary()
print('PASS')
testCases.description: Correctness on the canonical input. Runs the tool against `orders-healthy.json` and checks the whole screen: header `active=iad ready=True degraded=False(Healthy)`, the writable primary rendered as `LAG unknown` and `SERVING no`, both followers `SERVING yes`, `VERDICT: OK`, exit code 0.

testCases.description: Catches a shortcut: applying one lag rule to every site and folding site lag into group health. Two fixtures, both with a site 300s behind a 30s threshold. In `orders-reader-soaking.json` the `read-only` reader is behind — the group must exit 0 while the reader shows `SERVING no`. In `orders-candidate-lagging.json` the `primary-candidate` replica is behind — the group must exit 1 while that replica shows `SERVING yes`. A uniform lag gate, or a verdict derived from the site rows, gets one of the two backwards. This test also feeds a group whose `iad` site omits `spec.sites[].role`, which must default to `primary-candidate`.
